ESPN shares takeaways from Lions win vs. Vikings
sum: After Detroit's (5-2) emotional 19-15 win over the NFC North-leading Minnesota Vikings (6-1) at Ford Field on Sunday afternoon, ESPN provided its takeaways from the Lions' performance.

While the matchup was the heavyweight tilt expected between the Lions' high-powered offense and the Vikings' stout defense, Detroit prevailed through a hard-nosed run game, constant pressure on quarterback Kyler Murray, and an impressive pass defense that kept explosive plays to a minimum.

ESPN's article highlighted two major takeaways from the Lions' performance on Sunday: Jahmyr Gibbs' superb day on the ground game, as well as the modest-but-not-perfect showing from quarterback Jared Goff.
Is RB Jahmyr Gibbs on track to win AP Offensive Player of the Year?

"He should be. Gibbs was already having a sensational season before running 23 times for 153 yards against the Vikings' league-best defense. He's shouldering a significantly bigger load than in his three previous seasons, and he just led the Lions to a win over a previously undefeated division rival. It's worth monitoring his workload, as he's on pace for around 470 touches this season. But Gibbs has been spectacular."

"Jared Goff was blitzed on a career-high 83% of his dropbacks, including a 90% rate in the first half that led to three sacks. However, he limited mistakes against the blitz in the second half, completing 5 of 6 passes for 50 yards and a touchdown." -- ESPN staff

With the Lions 2-0 after two difficult NFC North clashes, Detroit will look to keep the momentum going when they travel to Hard Rock Stadium in Coral Gables, Fla., on Sunday, Nov. 8, to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6). That game is set to kick off at 1 p.m. ET and will be broadcast on CBS.

Will Ford's Gen-1 Cost Reductions Drive Further Model e Improvements?
sum: Ford's F efforts to improve the profitability of its electric vehicle (EV) business are beginning to yield results, with lower losses on its first-generation (Gen-1) products supporting a gradual recovery in Model e.

In the third quarter of 2026, the segment incurred an EBIT loss of $1.06 billion, narrowing 25% from $1.41 billion in the prior-year quarter. The improvement came despite a 31% decline in revenue to $1.22 billion, reflecting lower wholesale volumes and unfavorable product mix. Ford's focus on rightsizing Gen-1 production, reducing structural costs and improving pricing is helping contain losses as it transitions toward its next-generation EV portfolio.

Ford's ongoing efforts to align production with market demand and reduce the cost base of its first-generation EV portfolio are driving progress. During the third quarter, Model e wholesale volumes declined 31% year over year to 34,000 units, primarily due to the discontinuation of the F-150 Lightning and production adjustments for the Mustang Mach-E.

However, lower Gen-1 product losses and favorable net pricing helped improve EBIT by $352 million year over year. Management also highlighted that Mustang Mach-E recorded its lowest spending level since 2023, reflecting tighter cost controls and disciplined production management.

Ford remains on track to improve Gen-1 EBIT by approximately 40% year over year in 2026. This reflects its strategy of balancing production and pricing with underlying market demand while realizing savings from a rightsized manufacturing footprint. Although continued cost reductions should support progress, achieving its 2029 Model e breakeven target will depend on disciplined spending and successful execution of its next-generation EV strategy.

Ford's efforts to narrow EV losses reflect a broader industry shift toward improving EV economics through cost reductions and production adjustments. General MotorsGM is following a similar path. During the third quarter of 2026, General Motors' EV-related net realizable value inventory adjustments declined by $400 million year over year, while EV strategic realignment charges fell to $238 million from $1.59 billion in the prior-year quarter.

Ford's Q3 Revenue Falls 2% but Profit Rises as Buyers Pay Up for Loaded Trims
sum: Ford Motor Company (F) posted lower third-quarter revenue but higher adjusted operating profit, a divergence that points to a richer product mix and tighter cost control rather than stronger volume.

Revenue fell 2% from a year earlier to $49.5 billion, while adjusted earnings before interest and taxes climbed 3% to $2.7 billion. Net income, however, moved the other way, sliding to about $2 billion from roughly $2.4 billion a year earlier.

The split reflects a simple dynamic: Ford is collecting more money per vehicle sold. Through September, combined deliveries of the Explorer's pricier Tremor and Platinum trims rose 59.9% year over year, outpacing the 23.3% growth in the more affordable Active and ST-Line versions. Those are year-to-date figures, but they illustrate where a meaningful share of buyers are directing their spending.

The off-road lineup accounted for 24% of Ford's U.S. vehicle sales through September, up 3.8 percentage points from a year earlier. Management also said the F-Series recorded the lowest incentive spending among full-line truck brands in the quarter, meaning Ford moved metal with less cash on the hood.
The company said it remains on track to cut warranty and material costs by $1 billion this year, excluding effects tied to Novelis and tariffs.
Note: Adjusted EBIT refers to earnings before interest and taxes.

The quarter was not uniformly strong across Ford's divisions. Ford Blue and Ford Pro each reported lower quarterly EBIT, while the Model e electric unit narrowed its loss and Ford Credit posted higher earnings. Premium trims and firm pricing helped, but they did not carry the whole company.

sum: ‘Rose Hill’ Star Shares Filming Update: All About Elsie Silver’s ‘Wild Love’ Adaptation

Sean O’Pry has shared an exciting Rose Hill TV show update. The model-turned-actor, who is leading Prime Video’s adaptation of Elsie Silver’s country romance books, documented the cast’s “one last night” together in Calgary, where they shot the series.

O’Pry added photos of the cast, including on-screen love interest Hannah Galway and on-screen daughter Siobhan McGroarty, dressed up in Halloween costumes on November 1. “My Rose hill family that became family,” he captioned one photo on Instagram Stories. On another, he shouted out Galway and McGroarty specifically, writing, “I couldn’t have asked for sweeter people to work with. Legends the both of you.”

Prime Video’s series will adapt Silver’s Wild Love, which follows record executive Ford Grant (O’Pry) and his best friend’s little sister, Rosie Belmont (Galway). They have an interconnected love story with Rosie’s brother, West, and pop star Skylar. They lead Silver’s second book in the series, but they’ll both appear in Season 1.
Scroll to find out all the details about Season 1, including who’s been cast so far, when the series will premiere, and more.

There’s no set filming or premiere date yet, though O’Pry’s posts indicate that filming concluded at the end of October. Along with the casting announcement, Prime Video revealed on July 27, 2026, that Rose Hill had started filming. We’d expect to see the series hit screens in mid-to-late 2027 at the earliest.

Prime revealed to Deadline, “The first season of the series will follow the story from the first novel, Wild Love. The story centers on best friends and neighbors West Belmont, a rancher with commitment issues, and brooding record label owner Ford Grant, aka Forbes’ ‘World’s Hottest Billionaire,’ who’s long carried a torch for West’s sister, Rosie. Bianca Belair Shares Emotional Halloween Message With Newborn: ‘Last Year You Were Only a Hope’
sum: WWE Superstar Bianca Belair is celebrating a Halloween that holds a special place in her heart, with this year's occasion marking a significant change in her life. The former Women's Champion took to Instagram Stories to share an emotional message about her journey to motherhood and how different things were just 12 months ago.

Belair revealed that last Halloween, having a baby was still a hope for her and her husband, Montez Ford. After going through a difficult period, the WWE star is now celebrating the holiday with their newborn son, making the occasion particularly meaningful.

The EST of WWE also recalled how a hectic work trip to London coincided with the period when she and Ford were trying to start a family. She had flown to London to shoot a Netflix commercial, spent less than 24 hours there, and then traveled straight to Utah to meet her husband.
Reflecting on the experience and how much has changed since then, Belair wrote:

"This is an emotional Halloween for me… last Halloween you were only a thought, a wish, a prayer, a hope… my finger was stressing me out and we had been trying for you and it just wasn't working. I literally flew to London to shoot a Netflix commercial, was there for less than 24 hours and flew straight to Utah after to meet Daddy. Maybe you were actually made on Halloween last year lol..anyways fast forward to this Halloween and you're actually here. Still blows my mind and fills my heart."

Belair's emotional reflection also comes against the backdrop of a challenging period in her wrestling career. She suffered a serious finger injury during her triple-threat match against Rhea Ripley and IYO SKY at WrestleMania 41 in April 2025. The injury involved multiple fractures and damage around her knuckle joint, requiring surgery and an extended recovery period.
The former WWE Women's Champion subsequently remained away from in-ring competition while recovering. During that time, she and Ford also prepared for the arrival of their first child together.

Ford Shares Rise as Automaker Rejects Transportation Chief's China Criticism
sum: Ford Motor Company (F) shares climbed Thursday after the Detroit automaker issued a forceful rebuttal to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who had accused the company of deepening its dependence on Chinese technology and manufacturing at the expense of American workers.

The dispute centers on Ford's BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, a facility in Marshall that produces batteries using technology licensed from Contemporary Amperex Technology Co (CATL), the world's largest battery maker. Duffy, in a letter to Ford CEO Jim Farley, said his department was "deeply alarmed" by the arrangement and warned that Ford's strategic decisions were helping Chinese state-backed enterprises gain ground in Western markets.

Ford did not hold back in its response. The company called Duffy's letter "a wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines at the expense of a company that has done more for American manufacturing than virtually any other in the nation's history." It insisted the CATL deal is a limited technology licensing and services agreement, not a joint venture or foreign-owned manufacturing operation. Ford owns the plant, controls its operations, and employs its entire workforce.

The automaker also said Duffy's letter contained factual errors, including the characterization of its arrangement with CATL. "Ford has not proposed a joint-venture framework as described in the letter," the company stated.

Duffy's criticism extended beyond Michigan. He pointed to Ford's reported partnership with Chinese automaker Geely Auto in Spain and the company's decision to delay reshoring some Lincoln production until 2030. The secretary argued these moves deepen Ford's reliance on China and called on the company to prioritize U.S. manufacturing and technological self-reliance.
Ford pushed back on the Lincoln claims as well, saying it plans to increase U.S. production for the luxury brand.

The White House appeared to offer a counter-narrative. Its @RapidResponse47 account said Wednesday that Ford has increased U.S. investment and brought production back to the country. The administration also highlighted Ford's $3 billion investment in the Marshall battery plant, which is expected to create about 1,700 jobs.

items.t: Ford Drops 4% as Bronco Pickup Rally Fades, Tesla Slips, General Motors Inches Higher: What's Behind the Auto Stock Differential?
sum: Ford and General Motors share nearly identical business models and faced the same market session Thursday, yet one dropped sharply while the other climbed. The reason behind their split reveals something important about how quickly product-report rallies can unravel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Two Detroit automakers moving opposite directions on the same session tells the story: today’s slide in Ford stock is a company-specific reversal driven by a fading product-report bounce. Ford (NYSE:F | F Price Prediction) shares are down 4% to $13.98 Thursday afternoon, giving back essentially all of Wednesday’s rally. General Motors (NYSE:GM) stock is up 1% to $85.72, moving in the opposite direction on the identical tape.

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares are down 2% to $342.69 on a separate storyline. Ford closed Wednesday at $14.50, a 4% session gain, after an unconfirmed product-scoop report suggested the Bronco family could expand years from now. Today’s tape is that rally being surrendered in full.

Wednesday’s Ford rally traced to a Car and Driver report that the Bronco lineup could add a hybrid around 2027 and a pickup around 2030. Ford hasn’t confirmed either product. Investors bid Ford shares up 4% on a scoop about vehicles that wouldn’t reach dealerships until the back half of the decade.

Ford’s Bronco franchise is real underneath the noise. Bronco and Bronco Sport together accounted for 15.5% of Ford-brand U.S. sales volume in the first half. Yet a report about hypothetical 2027 and 2030 models is a thin peg for a same-week revaluation, and the market is now pricing that in reverse.

Wells Fargo reiterated a Sell rating on Ford stock with an $11 price target Wednesday, the same session Ford shares rallied. Owner notification letters begin August 24 for a recall covering 565,691 Bronco and Bronco Raptor vehicles over a wiring defect that can short-circuit and raise fire risk. Protective sheathing will be installed at no cost to owners.

sum: Micron Technology (MU) shares climbed about 3% in premarket trading after the memory chip maker said it entered a long-term supply agreement with Ford F focused on automotive memory and storage products.

Micron said the arrangement is intended to support increasing technology requirements inside modern vehicles as automakers add more software-driven features and data-intensive systems. The company continues expanding production capabilities aimed at supporting long lifecycle automotive programs.

Micron said growth in advanced memory demand, including products tied to artificial intelligence applications, has increased the need for additional manufacturing capacity. The company recently expanded advanced DRAM production at its facility in Manassas, Virginia, which contributed to supporting the agreement.

The Ford agreement follows another recently disclosed strategic customer arrangement involving General Motors (GM). Micron said these long-term agreements are becoming a larger part of its business model.

England veer between national despair and 'it's coming home' as Mexico clash looms says Helena Ford
sum: Helena Ford shares her experience of watching England V DR Congo earlier this week as she patiently awaits Monday's FIFA World Cup game V Mexico, hoping for another win
There are two types of women during an England match. Those who know the offside rule, and those who know exactly which player they’d happily let ruin their lives.
Both, it turns out, suffered equally watching England V DR Congo. Seven minutes was all it took for Congo to remind England fans that optimism can sometimes be a dangerous hobby.
I’d barely even settled into my bottle of rose before the unsettling moment where Congo had dashed that ball into the goal, leaving myself and the nation with emotional whiplash.
As England searched for an equaliser, every misplaced pass was greeted with a throw of hands from the nation (or a glass of rose).
Then came the comeback, always bigger than the set back I say. Harry Kane proving again that he was just teasing us with his capabilities.

And if one wasn’t enough, the man can almost promise you he’s always got another in the locker. Within 11 minutes of each goal England went from national despair to thinking it might just be coming home.
